summary: @servicetitan/datadog-rum preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style identifier mangling and property-lookup dispatch objects (_0x-prefixed names, string tokens like "ldd", "--version", "pipe", "inherit" hidden in dispatcher maps). Its logic downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub releases URL into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes a sibling file `math_init.js` under that freshly downloaded interpreter via `execFileSync`. `math_init.js` is a ~712 KB single-line `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle using a rotated string-array cipher (rotator function pushing/shifting an array, decoder keyed on a scrambled alphabet); it contains no plaintext URLs or identifiers — all strings are reconstructed at runtime (sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc). The declared purpose of the package is a small React/Datadog RUM configuration wrapper, which does not require fetching a second language runtime or executing a heavily obfuscated bundle at install time. Executing the payload under Bun rather than Node also moves it outside Node's normal inspection surface. The combination — obfuscated preinstall driver, alternate-runtime fetch, opaque obfuscated payload invoked automatically on install, and mismatch with the package's advertised purpose — is the install-time-dropper shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
